items.title: machine-readable scheduling failure diagnostics for unscheduled Pods

items.body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to discuss whether Kubernetes should expose more structured, machine-readable scheduling failure diagnostics for Pods that cannot be scheduled.

Today, kube-scheduler reports scheduling failures through `FailedScheduling` Events and the `PodScheduled` condition. However, the detailed causes are primarily encoded in human-readable messages, for example:

```text
0/3 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu, 2 node(s) had untolerated taint ...
```

This is useful for humans, but difficult for automation and troubleshooting tools to consume reliably without parsing message strings.

This issue is intended to start a discussion before drafting a KEP. I understand that feature requests are unlikely to make progress as issues alone, and I plan to engage with SIG Scheduling on Slack and consider a KEP if the problem space is considered worth pursuing.

A possible direction could be to expose stable scheduling failure categories, for example:

```yaml
status:
  schedulingDiagnostics:
    result: Unschedulable
    reasonCodes:
    - InsufficientCPU
    - TaintMismatch
    failedPlugins:
    - NodeResourcesFit
    - TaintToleration
```

This is only an illustrative example. I am not proposing a final API shape in this issue.

Initial scope could be:

preserve the existing FailedScheduling Events
preserve the existing PodScheduled condition behavior
avoid changing scheduling decisions
avoid exposing per-node detailed failure data by default
define a generic diagnostics format that scheduler plugins could contribute to
avoid solving feature-specific diagnostics for Gang Scheduling, DRA, or preemption in the first step

Non-goals:

change scheduling semantics
introduce a new scheduling policy
replace existing Events
replace existing human-readable messages
expose sensitive or high-cardinality per-node scheduling details by default

Questions for SIG Scheduling:

Is this problem already covered by an existing KEP, issue, or ongoing work?
Would SIG Scheduling be interested in a generic structured diagnostics format for scheduling failures?
Should this start as a KEP, or would it be better to first prototype a smaller change in Events, Pod status, or scheduler framework status handling?
Which API surface would be most appropriate: Pod status, Events, or something else?

### Why is this needed?

Operators, SRE teams, and automation tools often need to understand why a Pod is Pending or unschedulable.

Today, many tools need to parse `FailedScheduling` Event messages or `PodScheduled` condition messages. This can be fragile because those messages are primarily designed for human readability, not as a stable machine-readable interface.

Structured scheduling diagnostics could help with:

- more reliable troubleshooting of Pending Pods
- better `kubectl` and dashboard experiences
- observability and AIOps integrations
- autoscaler and remediation tooling
- avoiding brittle parsing of scheduler event messages

I found some related areas, but I could not find a generic KEP that standardizes machine-readable scheduling failure diagnostics across scheduler plugins.

Related topics include:

- existing `FailedScheduling` Events
- existing `PodScheduled` condition with `reason: Unschedulable`
- scheduler framework plugin status
- Gang Scheduling failure handling
- DRA scheduling failures
- historical discussions around Pod failure reason visibility

This issue is meant to validate whether the problem is real and whether SIG Scheduling would be interested before any KEP is drafted.

/sig scheduling
/kind feature

items.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141403 needs to be merged first

Only dependency for scheduler is ```NoteLengthLimit```, we can create our own const, if value for this will change it will increase, so we should be safe with having our own const for this. Or we can check if there is a good place in staging to put it for general use.

Any ```k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core/validation``` entry in the allow-list added by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141415 should be removed in the same PR.
 
/sig scheduling
